EPMC:PMC:PMC8524584.topic: Total hip replacement for intracapsular hip fracture
EPMC:PMC:PMC8524584.setting: Kings Mill Hospital, district general hospital (Sherwood Forest Trust)
EPMC:PMC:PMC8524584.standard: NICE hip fracture guideline eligibility criteria for THR vs hemiarthroplasty; BOA COVID-19 guidance on management of urgent orthopaedic conditions and trauma

cycle1.result: THR compliance dropped during the peak COVID months from 35% to 21.4%; Kings Mill THR compliance 27.3% vs national 18.3%; 54.5% of eligible patients were operated on by THR-performing consultants but received hemiarthroplasty.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524584.intervention: Planned introduction of a new table in the clerking booklet to identify THR-eligible patients, with re-audit.
EPMC:PMC:PMC8524584.other_findings: Length of acute admission fell from 10 days to 8 days.

PMID:26924483.setting: Musgrave Park Hospital, large elective orthopaedic unit with onsite bone bank
PMID:26924483.standard: General Medical Council guidance on consent; documentation of consent for allograft use

cycle1.result: 17/45 cases (38%) had adequate preoperative documentation or an appropriately completed consent form for planned allograft use.

PMID:26924483.other_findings: Revision hip arthroplasty was the main allograft user (48%); little correlation between surgeon allograft use frequency and consent adequacy (correlation coefficient -0.12).

PMID:3508849.setting: Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology, University Central Hospital, Helsinki

cycle1.result: Mean kyphosis 14 degrees on admission, 5 degrees postoperatively and 12 degrees at follow-up; neural improvement in 28 patients (34% of those with a deficit); complications in 29 patients.

PMID:3508849.other_findings: Case series of Harrington instrumentation; radiographic results better in thoracic and thoracolumbar injuries than lumbar.

PMID:20663276.topic: Time to specialist review for acute knee injury
PMID:20663276.setting: Sports clinic / Acute Knee Clinic, University College Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Average of five visits of any sort before specialist review.

PMID:20663276.intervention: Introduction of a weekly open-access Acute Knee Clinic.

cycle2.result: 89% reduction in time to diagnosis for A&E referrals and 32% reduction for GP referrals; average one visit before specialist review.

PMID:42219181.topic: Infection after foot and ankle surgery

cycle1.result: Superficial infection 4.1% (n = 397/9,591) and deep infection 1.4% (n = 133/9,591).

PMID:42219181.other_findings: Infection rates were significantly higher after acute diabetic surgery; deep infection higher in trauma than elective surgery; comorbidities and smoking affected infection rate.

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:9429956.intervention: Multidisciplinary working group developed nursing care protocols/pathways for fractured neck of femur.
PMID:9429956.other_findings: Authors report clearer patient flow, increased awareness of responsibilities and reduced duplication of effort, without numerical results.

PMID:20204376.topic: Redo urethroplasty after pelvic fracture urethral injury
PMID:20204376.setting: Department of Urology, Christian Medical College, Vellore

cycle1.result: Successful result in 36 (83.72%), improved and stable in five, failure in two.

PMID:20204376.other_findings: Number of previous attempts and stricture length did not affect outcome; failures usually within the first 3 months.

PMID:39759464.setting: Royal Oldham Hospital, Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:39759464.standard: BOA standardised list of risks for NOF fracture procedures

cycle1.result: Average of only 56.6% of risks included on each consent form; significant risks such as mortality frequently missed.

PMID:39759464.intervention: Stickers for consent forms and team education sessions.
PMID:39759464.other_findings: Authors recommend a further cycle to check sustainability.

PMID:20615300.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro

cycle1.result: Non-union 6.2%; screw irritation and removal 20.7%.

PMID:20615300.intervention: Selection criteria modified with age limit of 50 years recommended for the trochanteric flip approach.

cycle2.result: Non-union 1.3%; no non-unions under age 50; screw irritation and removal 28.3%.

PMID:20615300.other_findings: Non-union increased with age; combined screw irritation incidence 22.4%.

PMID:23571394.setting: Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford, specialist centre
PMID:23571394.standard: Documentation of risks and complications on consent forms for primary hip replacement

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:23571394.intervention: Procedure-specific complication stickers for consent forms.

cycle2.result: 86 consent forms used the sticker; significant improvement in documentation of fracture, neurovascular damage, leg length discrepancy, failure, loosening, death, medical complications, pain, stiffness, wound problems and other (P<0.0001).

cycle1.result: 81% of 531 non-operatively managed patients instructed for early weight-bearing; only 21% of 276 operatively managed patients.

PMID:30933870.other_findings: Notable variability between and within hospitals for operatively managed fractures.

EPMC:PPR:PPR339496.topic: Fascia iliaca block in hip fracture
EPMC:PPR:PPR339496.standard: Administration of fascia iliaca compartment block to hip fracture patients

cycle1.result: not reported

EPMC:PPR:PPR339496.intervention: Results presented at departmental and mortality meetings; teaching sessions for doctors; encouraged use of the neck of femur proforma to document FICB or a valid reason for omission.

cycle2.result: Statistically significant increase in patients receiving fascia iliaca block (p value not given in abstract).

EPMC:PMC:PMC3102974.setting: High risk foot unit, Liverpool Hospital, NSW

cycle1.result: Coliform colonisation 83 (63.4%), Staphylococcus aureus 57 (43.5%), MRSA 21 (16%), streptococcus 14 (10%).

EPMC:PMC:PMC3102974.other_findings: Authors concerned by high MRSA incidence.

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:42696559.other_findings: Review article on the global care gap in fragility fracture management.

PMID:7719180.topic: Hip fracture mortality and process of care
PMID:7719180.setting: All eight hospitals in East Anglia with trauma orthopaedic departments

cycle1.result: 560 (97%) treated surgically; 261 (45%; range 10-91%) received pharmaceutical thromboprophylaxis; 502 (93%; 81-99%) antibiotic prophylaxis; 90-day mortality 18% (5-24% between hospitals).

PMID:7719180.other_findings: One hospital had significantly better survival (OR 0.14; 95% CI 0.04-0.48; P = 0.0016); fatal PE differed by DVT prophylaxis (P = 0.001).

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383534.setting: Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow, Major Trauma Centre
EPMC:PMC:PMC9383534.standard: Departmental guidance to specify COVID-19 as a risk on trauma and orthopaedic consent forms

cycle1.result: 49% of consent forms specified COVID-19 as a risk.

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383534.intervention: Data presented at departmental governance meeting and an infographic disseminated to all clinicians.
EPMC:PMC:PMC9383534.other_findings: Indicative perioperative COVID-19 risk fell from 2.15% (2 positives) to less than 1% (no positives).

EPMC:PMC:PMC8030224.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic department, Bristol Royal Children's Hospital, tertiary referral centre
EPMC:PMC:PMC8030224.standard: BOAST COVID-19 standards (management of patients with urgent orthopaedic conditions and trauma during the coronavirus pandemic)

cycle1.result: Patient-initiated follow-up 16% in acute fracture clinic and 12% in fracture follow-up clinic.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8030224.intervention: Pandemic service changes including a virtual fracture clinic, patient-initiated follow-up, reduced radiography and cancellation of elective operating.

cycle2.result: Acute fracture clinic and follow-up bookings reduced by 40% and 48%; patient-initiated follow-up rose to 75% and 35%; only 17% and 39% needed radiographs.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8030224.other_findings: On-call referrals and trauma cases fell by almost 50%; all elective operating cancelled in 2020.

PMID:15206512.setting: Hospitals in the Oxford region (9 of 10 responded)

cycle1.result: 78% knew of a pre-admission screening policy; 15% unaware of any MRSA policy; teicoplanin 44% and vancomycin 44% for prophylaxis; 18% believed cefuroxime used; 48% of hospitals had an MRSA-free zone.

PMID:15206512.other_findings: Postal questionnaire with overall individual response rate 67.5% (27/40); re-audit after uniform policy proposed.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8153828.topic: Non-hip femoral fracture care in older patients
EPMC:PMC:PMC8153828.standard: BOAST/NICE: surgery within 36 hours, orthogeriatric assessment within 72 hours, documented ceiling of treatment, falls risk assessment, bone health review, nutritional assessment, physiotherapy review

cycle1.result: Versus neck of femur fractures: surgery within 36 hours 63.9% vs 66%; orthogeriatric assessment within 72 hours 32.6% vs 91.9%; falls risk 76.7% vs 99.6%; bone health 41.9% vs 99.7%; nutrition 55.8% vs 99.6%; physiotherapy 97.7% vs 98.9%.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8153828.intervention: Planned proforma for all femoral fractures and presentation to orthogeriatric, bone health and physiotherapy teams, with re-audit.
EPMC:PMC:PMC8153828.other_findings: Longer average length of stay (19 vs 14 days) and higher 30-day mortality (9.3% vs 8.6%).

PMID:22753670.setting: Charles Salt Centre, Robert Jones & Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic Hospital, Oswestry

cycle1.result: ONJ in 1 patient (0.5%); thigh pain 27 (13.4%); atypical femoral fracture in 4 (2%).

PMID:22753670.other_findings: All four AFF cases had long pamidronate treatment (median 12.5 years); IV bisphosphonate increased lumbar spine but not femoral neck BMD.

PMID:26868116.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance criteria for total hip replacement

PMID:33534280.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic trauma clinics, quaternary care hospital and three satellite sites, Boston

cycle1.result: 77 (11%) new patients did not bring previous X-rays, generating reimaging charges of $33,326 (30%-50% of total visit charges).

PMID:20542887.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust, Reading

cycle1.result: First-pass success in 184 insertions (38 of 42 by trainees); no failures of insertion or ventilation.

PMID:20542887.other_findings: No patient needed turning supine for an airway problem.

PMID:24428375.topic: Anaesthetic type and hip fracture mortality

cycle1.result: No significant difference between general and spinal anaesthesia in 5-day (2.8% vs 2.8%, p = 0.991) or 30-day (7.0% vs 7.5%, p = 0.053) mortality.

cycle1.result: 38% underwent arthroplasty with Hb <130; 14% with Hb <120; 11% of anaemias appropriately investigated; 7% had attempted treatment.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8153812.intervention: Results presented at clinical governance meeting; departmental action plans for early identification and treatment of anaemia to Hb 130, delaying operations where necessary.

cycle2.result: 21% operated with Hb <130 (p = 0.036); 0% with Hb <120; 80% of anaemias appropriately investigated (p < 0.001); attempted treatment 20% (p = 0.279).

PMID:29866427.setting: Emergency Department, Skåne University Hospital, Lund

cycle1.result: 25% of patients experienced some complication, mainly skin and cast-related problems; no severe complications.

PMID:29366541.setting: Musculoskeletal physiotherapy outpatients, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.dates: Phase one, one year (dates not reported)
cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:29366541.intervention: Phase two: strengthening as core treatment; phase three: standardised protocol of high load isometric exercise progressing to concentric and eccentric strengthening.
